answer: Each identity runs one lotus plot and locks an 80-credit bond. At dawn it collects lotus dew only at its vertex post and files its mass and serial. An auditor recomputes dew from the dawn dew-point table and checks the serial in the register. Deviation over 4 percent, a reused serial, or dew from two plots burns the bond. The first filing costs 37; the kth costs 37+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5032; 1000 fakes pay 2,534,500 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-plot ring fails: dew from the owner's vertex carries the owner's serial. An honest agent pays 37 once, bond returned after audit.
